standard.title: Automotive Vehicles — Electric Horns — Specification (Third Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the mechanical, electrical, and acoustical requirements, as well as methods of tests for 6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V electric horns for use in motor vehicles, including those intended for two and three wheelers.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the mechanical, electrical, and acoustical requirements, as well as methods of tests for 6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V electric horns for use in motor vehicles, including those intended for two and three wheelers.

version.current_version: Third Revision, 1993 (reaffirmed in 2026, incorporating Amendment No. 1, 2, 3, and Amendment No. 4, February 2026)

amendments.summary: Substitutes Clause 1 to expand the scope to cover 48 V electric horns, updates terminal testing voltage limits, restricts maximum connecting leads electrical resistance, and replaces legacy IS 9000 environmental test methods with contemporary IS/IEC 60068 standards.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Rule 119 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all electric horns fitted on motor vehicles, agricultural tractors, combine harvesters, and alternate fuel/battery vehicles must conform to IS 1884:1993 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified electric horns in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Every certified horn must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) legibly engraved or printed on the shell.
Specifies starting, mechanical, electrical, and acoustical limits for electric horns powered by standard direct current electrical systems rated at 6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V.

To prevent excessive voltage drops and maintain stable sound output, the electrical resistance of the connecting leads (excluding any switch contact in the circuit) must not exceed: a) 0.05 ohm for 6 V; b) 0.10 ohm for 12 V; c) 0.20 ohm for 24 V; and d) 0.40 ohm for 48 V.

When tested on an open site or in an anechoic chamber at a distance of 2 meters, the sound pressure level (A-weighted) must range between 105 dB(A) and 115 dB(A) for passenger/commercial vehicles (Roots Megasonic: 120 ± 5 dB(A), Uno Minda: 105-110 dB(A)), while remaining within legal RTO and CMVR limits.

During electrical and acoustical evaluations, the test voltage measured directly at the horn terminals must be maintained precisely at: a) 6.5 ± 0.2 V for 6 V horns; b) 13.0 ± 0.3 V for 12 V horns; c) 26.0 ± 0.5 V for 24 V horns; and d) 52.0 ± 1.0 V for 48 V horns.
Every horn must pass updated ingress protection and sealing tests per IS/IEC 60068-2-17 to verify that the solenoid coils and tungsten contact assemblies are fully waterproof.

Prior to mechanical testing, horns must undergo dry heat conditioning in accordance with IS/IEC 60068-2-2 to ensure thermal stability and prevent materials (such as bobbin plastic) from melting under engine bay heat.
Horns must survive extreme sub-zero environment exposures per IS/IEC 60068-2-1 without developing mechanical stiffness, spring fracturing, or sound damping.
The symbols, controls, and indicators associated with the horn must comply with the requirements of IS 15575 (1) and (2).

Electro-mechanical horns must be designed for a minimum endurance mission life of 100,000 cycles (continuous beep-rest intervals) under Indian standards, with modern high-durability variants tested up to 300,000 cycles without structural fatigue or contact wear.
